description: Scout connector telemetry, session-token accounting, the restrict_tools MCP gate and the two privacy gates. Activate only inside scout runs: SCOUT_MODE from the runner, or, for a session started inside a vault without a runner, the run mode its prompt names (scout/hooks/run_context.py). Interactive sessions are skipped by those. The PreToolUse restrict_tools gate is different: it applies to every session (run or interactive) in a vault whose connectors.custom.yaml uses restrict_tools, the vault being SCOUT_DATA_DIR, else the one containing the session's cwd as the payload gives it (as every Python hook finds it; never the hook process's own working directory, and a cwd the shell can't read for certain starts Python); it starts Python only when that file might set the key: the literal text, any backslash (a double-quoted YAML key can spell it with escapes, #590) or a NUL byte, and Python then decides on the parsed file. Elsewhere it exits before starting Python. When the gate cannot start (no venv, a shim naming a missing interpreter, a crash before the gate, an engine half-replaced mid-upgrade: any exit but 0, since the gate itself always exits 0), the call is blocked (exit 2, naming /scout-update and scoutctl bootstrap doctor) in a session that may be in a vault (SCOUT_DATA_DIR, or a scout-config.yaml at or above the payload's cwd; a cwd the shell can't read for certain counts as in one), and left with a non-blocking exit 1 everywhere else; with prefilter.sh missing too, the entry decides on SCOUT_DATA_DIR and its own working directory, since the payload has gone to the engine. The privacy gates (#453) count a session as a scheduled run by #517's rule (SCOUT_MODE set, or SCOUT_READER set to anything but exactly owner). kb-read-gate denies a run's shell/Grep/Glob read of knowledge-base/ and action-items/context/ in favour of scoutctl kb (Read stays allowed; an agent:* reader is denied it, and a delegate:<id> reader (#550) is denied a Read of any vault file scoutctl kb wouldn't show it, KB or not, so the Read hook sends every delegate Read to Python); It also denies a run's Bash call that sets, unsets or blanks SCOUT_MODE or SCOUT_READER or clears the environment (env -i), or that sets, unsets or exports HOME to anything but itself, or gives a builtin that sets what it names a name built at run time (the gate expands ~ and $HOME with the run's own HOME; once quotes and backslashes are removed, any command that mentions HOME, or the name of such a builtin, repeat or (( anywhere, goes to Python), or that sets or exports XDG_CONFIG_HOME (git's global config dir), or that detaches (nohup, setsid, disown, a trailing &, launchctl, osascript, open, tmux, screen, script, at, batch, ssh) (#595); the commit hook knows a run's commits from the process table whatever their environment says. It also denies, names and records (event kb_read_gate.hook_skip) a run's git call that skips or redirects the commit hooks: --no-verify or -n where it means that, -c or --config-env or git config on core.hooksPath, alias.* or include.path, GIT_CONFIG_* variables, commit-tree, update-ref on a branch, and a Bash write into .git/hooks or .git/config (#607). It exits in the shell for every other session, and for a run's Bash call that names no KB path, and whose command value has no run-env, detach or hook-skip word, no `scoutctl kb` call feeding xargs, a loop, read or a command substitution, no recursive read (rg, ag, ack, fd, ugrep, their aliases ug, fdfind and ack-grep, find, tree, du, ls -R, git grep), no grep at all (a run's grep is Claude Code's ugrep, which reads a folder it is given without -r), no recursive copy, archive or compare (diff -r, pax, zip, cpio, ditto, scp, gzip, zstd, lz4), no word the shell rewrites into another path (a glob character, a $ other than $?, $#, $! and $$, a backtick, a brace list, a leading ~, an absolute path, a ( for zsh alternation), no xargs or parallel and no cd into action-items (in any letter case, quoted or not), no cwd in or under action-items, and no KB path in any letter case once its quotes and backslashes are removed, for grep to find. A run's Grep, Glob or Bash payload over 32 KB is blocked in the shell: checking a longer one could outlast the hook's timeout, and a hook that times out allows the call. Since the 2026-11 KB audit it also denies a read through a variable or loop holding a KB path, one xargs feeds with KB paths, an input redirection from a KB path, a quoted program (sh -c, eval) that reads the KB, and a recursive read rooted at the vault or above. kb-write-gate (its own hook name, so an engine that predates it fails closed: exit 2) denies a run's Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit into what decides which hooks run (Phase 1b of spec 2026-11-13; scout/kb/hook_paths.py): the vault's git dir (all of it, a worktree's real git dir too), the user's git config (~/.gitconfig, ~/.config/git, $GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL), the agent's settings.json/settings.local.json in the vault's .claude, ~/.claude and $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, its plugin store, and the hook config dirs of other agent CLIs (.codex, .gemini, .agents, .grok, .cursor), after resolving ~, .. and symlinks and ignoring case; a run's Bash write to those agent and git-config paths is denied the same way. Every run write goes to Python (about 40 ms), since a symlink can hide the path from the shell; owner sessions exit in the shell. Both record kb_read_gate.hook_skip. Round 3 of #637: a run's shell write to a path the gate can't work out (a command substitution, a backtick, or a variable set elsewhere) is denied; an inline program (an interpreter's -c or -e program, or a here-document fed to one) is judged only when it writes files or starts programs, by the paths and protected names its own text spells; a shell that runs its stdin (sh <<EOF, | bash) is judged on those commands. Scout's secrets (~/.scout-secrets, $SCOUT_SECRETS_DIR) and the vault's delegate state (.scout-state/delegate-mirrors.json, .scout-state/delegate-scan/, .scout-state/delegate-inbox/) are write-protected, the agents' inbox copies (.scout-inbox/agents/) are read- and write-protected; a run's Read, Grep or Glob of the secrets is denied (the Read hook starts Python in a run when the payload names scout-secrets or $SCOUT_SECRETS_DIR), and a Bash read is denied when the command spells a secret's path (best effort), except the Telegram bot token and chat id. kb-read-label (PostToolUse on Read) attaches the note's privacy label (private: never to a shared surface) in any vault session; it exits in the shell unless the payload names a KB path, and labels a note it can't classify as private. shared-read-record (PostToolUse on Agnes's three shared-notes tools) records what the answer showed in .scout-cache/shared-reads/, so check-outbound recognises it, and tells the session the rule for it; a session in no vault (by the payload's cwd) that isn't a run exits in the shell. front-page-reads (PostToolUse on a run's Write, Edit or MultiEdit) warns, never blocks, when the file is a project's front page (<projects_dir>/<name>/<name>.md) and the session's transcript (and its subagents') shows no read of a note under that project's knowledge/ folder; it names only notes the run's reader may see, marks private ones, exits in the shell for owner sessions and for a payload whose file_path isn't shaped <dir>/<x>/<x>.md, starts Python only then, and always exits 0. outbound-gate runs check-outbound on an MCP write tool's input in a vault (Slack as surface slack, others as connector_write): a run is denied, the owner is warned; a session in no vault (by the payload's cwd) that isn't a run exits in the shell. Both fail closed for runs (exit 2 when scoutctl can't run). Per #72, per-tool-call accounting was moved out of PostToolUse (which fired one Python cold-start per tool call) into the session-tool-log Stop hook that walks the transcript once at session end. The shell stage of every tool hook lives in hooks/prefilter.sh (one named filter per entry; the Bash pattern is one commented alternation group per concern). Each entry here only starts it with /bin/sh by absolute path and names the Python hook it may reach. The run-only entries test for a run first, so an owner session leaves before any program starts. The script ends every filter with exit 200 + the hook's code, and an entry trusts nothing else: if prefilter.sh is missing, empty, broken or a no-op, the entry starts the Python hook directly; if it is killed, a gate entry blocks a run's call (exit 2) and otherwise starts the Python hook.

hooks.command: h="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/prefilter.sh"; c="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/engine/bin/scoutctl"; s=0; if [ -s "$h" ] && [ -r "$h" ]; then /bin/sh "$h" mcp-tool-gate "$c" hook mcp-tool-gate; s=$?; [ "$s" -ge 200 ] && exit $((s - 200)); fi; [ "$s" -ge 128 ] && { [ -n "$SCOUT_MODE" ] || { [ -n "${SCOUT_READER+set}" ] && [ "$SCOUT_READER" != owner ]; }; } && { echo "[scout:mcp-tool-gate] Scout's hook pre-filter failed (exit $s), so this call is blocked in a scheduled run." >&2; exit 2; }; "$c" hook mcp-tool-gate && exit 0; s=$?; d="$PWD"; [ -z "$SCOUT_DATA_DIR" ] || d=; while [ "${d#/}" != "$d" ] && [ ! -f "$d/scout-config.yaml" ]; do [ "$d" = / ] && exit 1; d="${d%/*}"; d="${d:-/}"; done; echo "[scout:mcp-tool-gate] Scout's MCP tool gate could not start (status $s), so this call is blocked in a vault. Run /scout-update or \`scoutctl bootstrap doctor\`." >&2; exit 2

h="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/prefilter.sh"; c="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/engine/bin/scoutctl"; s=0; if [ -s "$h" ] && [ -r "$h" ]; then /bin/sh "$h" outbound-gate "$c" hook outbound-gate; s=$?; [ "$s" -ge 200 ] && exit $((s - 200)); fi; if [ "$s" -lt 128 ] || ! { [ -n "$SCOUT_MODE" ] || { [ -n "${SCOUT_READER+set}" ] && [ "$SCOUT_READER" != owner ]; }; }; then "$c" hook outbound-gate; s=$?; [ "$s" -eq 0 ] && exit 0; fi; [ -n "$SCOUT_MODE" ] || { [ -n "${SCOUT_READER+set}" ] && [ "$SCOUT_READER" != owner ]; } || exit 1; [ "$s" -eq 2 ] || echo "[scout:outbound-gate] Scout's hook pre-filter or gate failed (exit $s), so this call is blocked in a scheduled run." >&2; exit 2

[ -n "$SCOUT_MODE" ] || { [ -n "${SCOUT_READER+set}" ] && [ "$SCOUT_READER" != owner ]; } || exit 0; h="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/prefilter.sh"; c="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/engine/bin/scoutctl"; s=0; if [ -s "$h" ] && [ -r "$h" ]; then /bin/sh "$h" kb-read-gate "$c" hook kb-read-gate; s=$?; [ "$s" -ge 200 ] && exit $((s - 200)); fi; [ "$s" -lt 128 ] && { "$c" hook kb-read-gate; s=$?; [ "$s" -eq 0 ] && exit 0; }; [ "$s" -eq 2 ] || echo "[scout:kb-read-gate] Scout's hook pre-filter or gate failed (exit $s), so this call is blocked in a scheduled run." >&2; exit 2

[ -n "$SCOUT_MODE" ] || { [ -n "${SCOUT_READER+set}" ] && [ "$SCOUT_READER" != owner ]; } || exit 0; h="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/prefilter.sh"; c="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/engine/bin/scoutctl"; s=0; if [ -s "$h" ] && [ -r "$h" ]; then /bin/sh "$h" kb-read-gate-read "$c" hook kb-read-gate; s=$?; [ "$s" -ge 200 ] && exit $((s - 200)); fi; [ "$s" -lt 128 ] && { "$c" hook kb-read-gate; s=$?; [ "$s" -eq 0 ] && exit 0; }; [ "$s" -eq 2 ] || echo "[scout:kb-read-gate] Scout's hook pre-filter or gate failed (exit $s), so this Read is blocked in a scheduled run." >&2; exit 2

[ -n "$SCOUT_MODE" ] || { [ -n "${SCOUT_READER+set}" ] && [ "$SCOUT_READER" != owner ]; } || exit 0; h="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/prefilter.sh"; c="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/engine/bin/scoutctl"; s=0; if [ -s "$h" ] && [ -r "$h" ]; then /bin/sh "$h" kb-write-gate "$c" hook kb-write-gate; s=$?; [ "$s" -ge 200 ] && exit $((s - 200)); fi; [ "$s" -lt 128 ] && { "$c" hook kb-write-gate; s=$?; [ "$s" -eq 0 ] && exit 0; }; [ "$s" -eq 2 ] || echo "[scout:kb-write-gate] Scout's hook pre-filter or gate failed (exit $s), so this write is blocked in a scheduled run." >&2; exit 2

h="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/prefilter.sh"; c="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/engine/bin/scoutctl"; s=0; if [ -s "$h" ] && [ -r "$h" ]; then /bin/sh "$h" kb-read-label "$c" hook kb-read-label; s=$?; [ "$s" -ge 200 ] && exit $((s - 200)); fi; exec "$c" hook kb-read-label

h="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/prefilter.sh"; c="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/engine/bin/scoutctl"; s=0; if [ -s "$h" ] && [ -r "$h" ]; then /bin/sh "$h" shared-read-record "$c" hook shared-read-record; s=$?; [ "$s" -ge 200 ] && exit $((s - 200)); fi; exec "$c" hook shared-read-record

[ -n "$SCOUT_MODE" ] || { [ -n "${SCOUT_READER+set}" ] && [ "$SCOUT_READER" != owner ]; } || exit 0; h="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/prefilter.sh"; c="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/engine/bin/scoutctl"; s=0; if [ -s "$h" ] && [ -r "$h" ]; then /bin/sh "$h" front-page-reads "$c" hook front-page-reads; s=$?; [ "$s" -ge 200 ] && exit $((s - 200)); fi; "$c" hook front-page-reads; exit 0
